newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait could renew AOC neutral zone right.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait could renew AOC neutral zone right.

text.p: Kuwait is leaning towards renewing Neutral Zone drilling rights for Japan's Arabian Oil Co Ltd (AOC) but a final decision has yet to be made, Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi said in remarks published on Tuesday.
"So far a final decision on renewal for AOC has not been taken," Mazeedi told al-Watan in an interview.
But oil ministry officials have made some proposals "the best of which was to continue giving the concession to AOC, that has been decided in view of Kuwait's supreme interest," he added.

AOC's concessions with Kuwait and Saudi Arabia in the Neutral Zone expire in 2003 and 2000 respectively. The two Gulf Arab OPEC heavyweights share the output from onshore and off-shore fields in the border area zone.

Japan imports five percent of its oil needs, 200,000 barrels per day (bpd), from the zone, another five percent from Kuwait and 20 percent from Saudi Arabia. The United Arab Emirates is Japan's main supplier with 27 percent.

AOC, which operates off-shore fields in the zone, plans to raise output to 350,000 barrels per day by the end of the century from around 300,000 bpd. A majority of AOC stock is held by Japanese interests but Kuwait and Saudi Arabia each hold a 10 percent stake in the firm.
Mazeedi said AOC was notified of "a primary approval on the possibility of studying the renewal of the concession agreement."
Onshore fields are shared by Saudi Arabian Texaco and the state Kuwait Oil Company (KOC).

Kuwaiti officials were quoted in October as saying that Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Saudi Arabian Texaco had agreed to spend $400 million to raise output from the onshore fields in the zone to 300,000 bpd by 1998 from 190,000-200,000 bpd.
Kuwait and Riyadh have shared the mineral rights to the zone equally since its establishment in 1922 by the sultanate of Nejd, now part of Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait, then a British protectorate.
